r2-building-01.observations: Roof shingles retain fine orange highlights, dark recessed grooves and rounded relief at the reference's dot scale. Plaster has dense small flecks, with compatible brown framing, shaded wooden entry and dark window. Ridge highlights and eave shadows fit the original lighting.

r2-building-02.observations: The steep roof preserves granular tiles, bright amber relief on its left plane and darker orange-purple recesses on its right. Gable and both facade levels retain fine plaster speckling and original-scale framing. Window, wooden entry and eave shading remain compatible with the reference.

r2-building-03.observations: Main and projecting roofs retain detailed orange shingles with small highlights and deep tile grooves. The cream walls and triangular gable keep the reference's plaster flecks and brown timber scale. Brighter left roof faces, darker right faces and eave shadows remain coherent through the roof junction.

r2-building-04.observations: The broad hipped roof maintains dense, relieved shingles rather than coarse flat cells. Both wall levels preserve fine plaster grain, narrow brown framing and detailed dark windows. Warm ridge and left-plane highlights, darker right roofing and shaded eaves match the established rendering.

r2-building-05.observations: Roof tiles preserve fine orange relief and dark grooves. The facade uses irregular pink-mauve stones with small highlights, chips and dark mortar compatible with the original sheet's masonry. Stone remains consistent around the window and wooden entry; roof-plane and eave shading fit the reference.

issues.reason: Large repeated cells and sparse tan dashes replace the reference's dense small shingles, curved highlights and recessed tile relief.
Broad smooth cream panels and heavy rectangular framing lack the original's fine plaster flecks and nuanced timber texture.
Muted tan, brown and gray-green ramps flatten internal material contrast, especially in the wood and openings, compared with the reference's richer shadow and highlight separation.
The shaded roof edge retains a conspicuous pale contour highlight. This perimeter treatment substitutes graphic outlining for the reference's localized, plane-following tile highlights.

sample-11.observations: The roof has a coarse repetitive dash grid inside a thick rim. Walls are mostly smooth beige areas with boxed windows, flat wood and a blocky base strip. Some right-plane darkening is visible, but the simplified relief, muted contrast and bright perimeter produce a graphic toy appearance.

r2-building-06.observations: The broad roof preserves dense orange tile highlights, dark recessed seams, and the reference's native grain scale. Plaster retains fine mottling within narrow timber framing. Chimney shading and eave shadow remain compatible; one wooden entry is visible.

r2-building-07.observations: Small highlighted tile crowns distinguish the bright left roof plane from the darker orange plane. Both the plaster gable and lower facade retain fine stippling and appropriately sized framing. The square gable opening is a window; one ground-level wooden door is visible.

r2-building-08.observations: Roof tiles retain the original stone building's granular relief and differentiated plane lighting. The taller masonry body uses small irregular stone marks, mottled interiors, and fine mortar at the established scale. The horizontal floor division does not enlarge the grain; one lower wooden door is visible.

r2-building-09.observations: The church matches the original sheet's bright upper blue tile courses, darker granular lower roof, and finely textured spire. Masonry preserves the original small stone clusters and cream-purple contrast. The yellow tower feature is glazing, and the sole wooden door is at ground level.

r2-building-10.observations: The candidate preserves the original stone house's rounded yellow-orange tile relief, darker right roof plane, speckled stone gable, and finely mottled masonry. Outline scale, palette, and shadows match the original sheet. One wooden entry is visible.

r3-building-01.observations: The main roof and projecting gable retain dense shingles with small rounded highlights and dark grooves. Plaster has fine irregular speckles and thin timber framing. Warm colors, brighter left roof faces, and eave shadows fit the references.

r3-building-02.observations: Both ochre gables have tightly packed tile courses, small highlights, and shaded grooves; the rear red roofing retains comparable grain. Plaster speckles and timber outlines remain at reference scale. Roof highlights consistently favor the left-facing planes.

r3-building-03.observations: The main roof and awning preserve dense red-and-ochre shingle relief. Exposed plaster retains fine dots and thin timber seams; the wooden counter has restrained horizontal shading. Colors and roof/eave lighting remain compatible with the original.

r3-building-04.observations: The olive roof retains granular shingles, pale highlights, and a darker right slope. Plaster speckles and fine brown framing match the reference scale. The changed roof color preserves sufficient relief and compatible lighting.

r3-building-05.observations: The blue tower roof has fine clustered shingles and bright left-edge accents; the orange chapel roof retains dense tile relief. Both wall sections use small irregular pink-gray stones and dark mortar. These materials and their directional shading match the reference sheet.

r3-building-06.observations: Both roof sections retain dense, small shingles with rounded relief and highlights following their slopes. Plaster has fine scattered grain; timber edges, warm colors, and shading match the originals.

r3-building-07.observations: The tall gables and connecting roof preserve granular shingles, bright tile lips, and darker opposing planes. Walls retain original-scale plaster flecks and timber contrast. The ground between wings visibly remains outdoors; only one wooden entry is visible.

r3-building-08.observations: Orange and slate-blue roofs both have dense individual shingle facets and directional highlights. The blue recoloring preserves texture relief. Fine plaster speckling, narrow framing, and window shading remain compatible with the reference.

r3-building-09.observations: The rounded cap contains tightly packed shingle grain with lighter upper-left areas and darker lower edges. Tapered plaster retains small irregular flecks, and the stone footing has fine masonry detail. Muted roof colors retain sufficient relief and compatible lighting.

r3-building-10.observations: The tan main roof retains dense rounded shingle marks, bright upper lips, and dark recesses; the orange entry roof uses compatible grain. Plaster flecks and timber outlines remain at the original dot scale. Both roof palettes preserve coherent highlight direction.

r6-building-01.observations: Brown shingles retain dense staggered light and dark clusters with visible tile relief. Plaster panels and the gable retain fine multitone specks; timber outlines match the reference scale. Roof shading darkens toward the right. One central wooden entry is visible.

r6-building-02.observations: The slate blue roof has tightly staggered shingles with small highlights and dark overlapping edges. Both facade levels preserve fine plaster grain and reference-sized timber framing. Roof shading is compatible with the upper-left light. The ground-floor wooden door is the only visible entry.

r6-building-03.observations: Ochre shingles have granular highlights, staggered dark edges, and a bright upper course. Stone walls retain small irregular blocks, fine internal variation, and narrow mortar comparable to the original masonry. Warm colors and lighting remain compatible. One wooden entry is visible.

r6-building-04.observations: The rounded olive roof retains dense overlapping tile marks and small relief highlights, with darker shading toward the right. Plaster speckling and dark timber framing match the original texture scale. The muted roof color fits the warm facade. One wooden entry remains unobstructed.

r6-building-05.observations: The blue conical roof shows dense staggered shingles with bright edges and dark tile feet. Tower plaster retains small multitone flecks, and the stone foundation has fine masonry grain. Right-side shading gives the tower volume without losing texture. One arched wooden entry is visible at the base.

r6-building-06.observations: The taupe roof retains dense staggered shingles with small highlights and dark overlaps at the reference's pixel scale. Plaster panels retain fine irregular speckles and narrow timber framing. Muted roof colors preserve relief, with compatible upper-left lighting and eave shadows.

r6-building-07.observations: The orange gable and olive wing show dense individual tile highlights, shaded overlaps and brighter left-facing surfaces. Walls retain fine pink-beige plaster grain. Timber, openings and roof shadows maintain contrast compatible with the originals.

r6-building-08.observations: The slate roof has granular shingle relief, a darker right hip and highlights that follow the roof planes. The orange annex retains multitone tile texture. Fine plaster speckles, timber shadows and dark accents remain consistent with the reference rendering.

r6-building-09.observations: The ochre bulb roof remains densely textured with small light caps and dark shingle recesses; courses change around the curved profile. Left-facing portions are brighter. The facade retains fine plaster mottling and reference-compatible brown framing and deep opening shadows.

r6-building-10.observations: Both rounded roofs retain dense small shingle marks, highlights and shaded overlaps. The tower has fine plaster flecks and a mottled stone footing; the house retains dotted plaster panels. Darker right edges and eaves provide compatible directional shading.

r7-building-01.observations: Orange shingles retain dense dark grooves and rounded yellow highlights consistent with the original stone house. Irregular stone courses preserve fine grain; window trim, outlines, and lighting remain compatible with the reference sheet.

r7-building-02.observations: The olive roof preserves small shingle highlights, granular shading, and dark tile separations at the original dot scale. Plaster panels retain fine scattered speckles and reference-sized timber framing. Ridge and left-plane highlights follow the roof geometry.

r7-building-03.observations: Both roof sections show dense orange shingles with pale raised edges and deep reddish shadow channels. The gable and timber facade retain fine plaster dots and narrow outlines. Highlight direction remains consistent across the upper and lower roofs.

r7-building-04.observations: Blue-gray wing roofs retain granular shingle relief and small directional highlights; the orange central roof uses compatible texture density. Fine plaster speckling continues across both stories. Timber and window outlines remain consistent with the originals, with coherent light across the roof planes.

r7-building-05.observations: The tall roof and descending wing preserve closely spaced orange tiles, rounded bright edges, and dark granular recesses. Plaster remains finely stippled throughout the framed facade. Warm roof colors, teal glazing, and directional shading fit the original rendering.

r7-building-06.observations: Slate roofing retains dense, small highlighted shingles and distinct hip-plane shading. Plaster has fine irregular stippling with reference-sized timber edges. Cool roofing, teal glass and warm wood remain compatible. One ground-level wooden door is visible.

r7-building-07.observations: Orange tower shingles and slate wing shingles retain granular relief with brighter left-facing roof planes. Masonry contains dense small stone faces, irregular joints and fine highlights comparable to the original stone buildings. Upper openings are glazed windows; one wooden entry is visible below.

r7-building-08.observations: Both gable roofs and the connecting roof show dense orange shingle grain, small yellow highlights and darker tile recesses. Plaster preserves fine dot texture and narrow timber detailing. Roof-plane lighting and facade contrast fit the references. One lower wooden door is visible.

r7-building-09.observations: The broad slate roof retains small alternating shingle highlights and dark joints throughout, with shading separating its roof planes. Wall panels retain the original fine plaster stipple and timber scale. Cool roof colors and warm facade contrast remain compatible. One ground-level entry is visible.

r7-building-10.observations: The ochre main roof and orange foreground gables retain dense granular shingles, discrete highlights and shaded recesses. Fine plaster dots and timber edges match the reference scale. Roof highlights consistently favor the upper-left and left-facing planes. One lower wooden door is visible.

r7-building-11.observations: The slate-blue roof retains dense staggered shingles with small highlights and dark recesses; the orange gable preserves rounded tile relief. Plaster has fine speckles and narrow timber boundaries. Contrast and roof-plane lighting fit the references.

r7-building-12.observations: Olive roofing remains granular, with individual shingle highlights and a darker right slope. The orange gable retains warm tile relief. Plaster speckling and timber contrast preserve the original dot scale and texture density.

r7-building-13.observations: Both orange gables and the blue-gray connecting roof retain dense small tile highlights and recesses. Stone walls show fine irregular masonry and mottled grain at the reference scale. Material contrast and directional lighting remain compatible.

r7-building-14.observations: Main and projecting roofs preserve dense orange-red shingle grain, golden highlights, and darker right-facing planes. Cream plaster retains small scattered dots and narrow dark timber boundaries. Texture scale, palette contrast, and lighting closely match the anchors.

r7-building-15.observations: The three orange gables carry dense rounded shingle relief; visible blue-gray roofing also retains fine grain. Plaster dots, timber edges, and teal glazing maintain reference-sized detail. Highlights and shadows agree across the roof planes.

issues.reason: The brown tower cap has extended parallel diagonal highlight chains with insufficient separation into rounded shingles. Its central and lower surface reads as striated weave rather than the reference's individually shaded tiles.

r7-building-16.observations: The olive house roof retains dense highlighted tile marks. Plaster has fine beige speckling, and the foundation has granular masonry. The brown cap's diagonal streaks are the material texture mismatch; its overall left-to-right shading is coherent.

r7-building-17.observations: The slate-blue cone has small staggered tile highlights and dark separations compatible with the original church roofing. Its right side is darker. The olive house roof preserves dense shingle relief; plaster speckles and granular stone footing remain at compatible pixel scale. One wooden entry is visible.

issues.reason: Both brown tower caps use parallel diagonal streaks that merge across multiple tile positions. The lower cap surfaces lack the distinct rounded shingle relief visible in the originals.

r7-building-18.observations: Both caps show the same striated brown texture. The central olive roof has finer separated tile marks. Cream plaster retains small mottled dots, and the stone bases retain fine masonry grain. Palette and broad lighting remain compatible.

issues.reason: The gold bulb roof's lower face is dominated by long diagonal light bands and zigzag weave. These bands suppress individual rounded tile faces and continue with nearly the same direction across the curved surface.

r7-building-19.observations: The orange wing roofs preserve granular original-looking shingles. Timber and plaster retain fine speckling and narrow dark joints. The gold upper roof has denser diagonal streaks than discrete shingle relief. Its broad left-side illumination is consistent with the surrounding roofs.

issues.reason: The gold cap's lower surface forms extended parallel diagonal highlights rather than individually shaded rounded shingles. The texture reads as striped weave across the bulb.

r7-building-20.observations: The orange foreground roof has fine bright tile tips and dark joints compatible with the reference. Plaster and timber retain original-scale grain. The gold cap's continuous diagonal bands are the material mismatch. The visible upper blue openings read as windows.

r7-building-21.observations: Slate, orange, and olive roofing retain dense small tile highlights and dark underlaps. Plaster preserves fine scattered flecks, with timber widths comparable to the reference. Bright left-facing orange tiles and shaded roof joins give compatible lighting.

r7-building-22.observations: Brown upper roofing and ochre lower roofing show closely spaced staggered tile relief rather than sparse bands. Fine plaster dots and timber detail match the reference scale. The upper roof darkens toward its right face, and the earthy colors remain compatible.

r7-building-23.observations: The broad olive roof retains dense shingle cells with small highlights and recessed dark marks, shading darker toward the right. All three facade levels retain fine plaster flecks and reference-scale timber lines. Window and balcony colors fit the warm plaster and wood.

r7-building-24.observations: The pointed slate roof and olive lower roof both have granular highlighted shingles and dark tile seams. Bright stepped tiles on the lower left slope and a darker right slope distinguish the roof planes. Plaster stippling and timber detail remain consistent across the facade.

r7-building-25.observations: The slate main roof has dense small shingle highlights and shadows; all three orange gables retain bright left-plane tile relief and darker right planes. Fine plaster flecks continue through the gables and lower walls. Timber outlines and warm facade contrast remain compatible with the originals.
